modules.title: Checked baggage
modules.lede: Qantas runs two allowance systems at once, and which one you get depends on where you're flying rather than what you paid.
body: Australian domestic flights and international flights to and from North and South America are counted by the piece — a set number of bags, each with its own weight cap. Everywhere else, including trans-Tasman, Asia, Europe and Africa, the allowance is a total weight you can split across as many bags as you like.

One rule catches out a lot of connecting passengers: if your international and domestic legs are on the same ticket, the international allowance applies to the domestic legs too. On separate tickets, domestic rules reassert themselves unless both tickets are presented at check-in and the connection falls within the same calendar day.

table.caption: Included checked allowance by route and cabin

rule.text: No single checked bag may exceed this, on any route, in any cabin. A 40 kg Business allowance is not permission to check one 40 kg bag — split it. Exceptions apply on smaller aircraft and a small number of routes.

conflicts.title: Figure under review
conflicts.text: Third-party sources report an airport excess fee of around A$161 per additional domestic piece and a 65 kg per-passenger cap on total checked baggage. Neither figure is confirmed against the published fee schedule, so the numbers are left out of the table above rather than printed and possibly wrong.

modules.title: Carry-on
body: Domestic passengers on jet services choose one of three configurations: one bag up to 115 cm total dimensions, or two bags up to 105 cm each, or one 105 cm bag plus a non-rigid garment bag. The two-bag options cap at 14 kg combined with no single piece over 10 kg. A small personal item — handbag, laptop sleeve — sits on top of all of them.
Dash 8 turboprop services are the exception, and the one worth remembering: a single bag, 105 cm, 7 kg. If any leg of your itinerary is on a Dash 8, pack to that limit rather than the jet limit.

Gate weighing is real, particularly on regional services where locker space runs short. Since every Qantas fare includes checked baggage, the practical answer to a borderline cabin bag is usually to check it.

conflicts.title: Sources disagree — international Economy weight
conflicts.text: The carrier's own carry-on page and several secondary sources give 10 kg for the single-bag international Economy option. Other reference sites give 7 kg and describe it as strictly enforced at the gate. The difference is one bag's worth of packing, so neither number is published until it can be pinned to the current conditions of carriage.

modules.title: What the cheapest fare includes
modules.lede: This is where Qantas diverges most sharply from the low-cost carriers it gets compared against on price.
body: A Qantas Economy fare at sale pricing still carries a checked bag — 23 kg domestically, 30 kg on most international routes. When you're comparing a Qantas fare against a low-cost headline price, that bag is often most of the gap, and the comparison isn't like-for-like until you add it back.
Some promotional fares do drop the checked allowance entirely, so the inclusion isn't universal — check the allowance shown on the review page before you pay, not the general policy.

modules.title: If your flight is delayed or cancelled
modules.lede: Which rules protect you depends entirely on where the flight departs — and on a Qantas ticket, that can change mid-itinerary.
body: Departing Australia, there is no fixed pay-on-delay scheme. Australia relies on Australian Consumer Law and the airline's own conditions of carriage, a weaker and less predictable position than European passengers hold.

Departing the EU, services fall under EU261 regardless of the carrier's nationality; departures from UK airports fall under UK261. Both cover delays past a set threshold, cancellations at short notice, and denied boarding.
Compensation amounts are deliberately not printed here until each figure is checked against the regulation text rather than against secondary coverage of it.

sources.label: Dept. of Infrastructure (AU), Aviation Consumer Ombuds Scheme
